Incident Bot: automated alert: latency_slo_burn detected for service=realtime-inference p95 and p99 crossing thresholds (>30m)
PagerDuty: PagerDuty incident created: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/P12345 - page: oncall_engineer
PagerDuty: page fired to: @alex-t, escalation to @jordan-l after 5m
Alex T: acked the page :white_check_mark: taking lead. seeing p95 ~ 1.1s, p99 ~ 3.4s on hosted-us-west cluster
Alex T: quick note — traffic spike from a PLG customer cohort plus a recent model roll (gptx-2q-compat) deployed to canary yesterday
Sam R: any errors or 5xx? Dashboard shows increased tail latency, error rate stable ~0.2% (no big 5xx spike)
Maria P: I can confirm KV cache miss rate jumped from 6% -> 45% around the same time. looks like cache TTL change from rollout? cc @alex-t
Alex T: pulling autoscaler and rollout diffs now. running `kubectl get deploy -n inference` then checking rollout history
Alex T: logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-04T15:12:02Z] request_latency p95=1100ms p99=3400ms active_reqs=2400 kv_cache_miss=0.45
[2026-03-04T15:12:12Z] backend_queue_len=1200 model_loads=13
```
Jordan L: if cache miss is main driver, we can flip TTL back. Do we control TTL at the routing layer or model-serving config?
Sam R: TTL changed in rollout v2.3.4 -> new default 10s (was 600s). I think the canary inherited wrong env var.
Maria P: confirmed: configmap `realtime-cache-config` updated in canary namespace at 15:05 UTC. key `prefix_ttl` bumped to 10s.
Alex T: mitigation plan: 1) revert configmap in canary -> set TTL back to 600s 2) scale up pool for 20m 3) enable fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint
Alex T: rolling revert now: `kubectl apply -f configmap-revert.yaml -n canary` — applying
Incident Bot: deployment event: configmap-revert applied by alex-t
Ops Bot: autoscaler actions: scaling `realtime-pool` from 60 -> 120 instances (spot + on-demand mix) triggered by manual scale
Alex T: scaled nodes and reverted TTL. monitoring... p95 dropped to 420ms within 3 minutes
Sam R: great. what about canary -> did we roll the wrong value to prod?
Maria P: canary had wrong var pushed via CI template. CI job `deploy-canary` used `cache-defaults:staging` accidentally. looks like template bug
Jordan L: assigning follow-up: Sam to fix CI template, Maria to run postmortem on config gating, Alex to file rollback blameless note and run smoke tests
Alex T: paging notes for ops: customers impacted: hosted API customers with high-rps connections saw increased latency; we observed ~12 customer sessions with elevated tail. support-ops notified.
PagerDuty: alert status: acknowledged by Alex T at 1769501238
Alex T: I'm handing off to Jordan in 20 min — will stay on thread for 10m overlap
Jordan L: taking over at 1769501258. continuing monitoring and verify canary -> prod not affected
Maria P: quick scoreboard: root cause = incorrect TTL env var in canary CI template -> cache thrash -> higher backend queueing -> p95/p99 SLO burn. Mitigation = revert TTL + scale up. Rollback = in-flight.
Sam R: next actions: 1) revert CI template default 2) add configmap validation step in pipeline 3) add alert mapping for sudden cache_miss increase
Alex T: filing incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-9821 with mitigation timeline and customer impact
Jordan L: closing notes: p95 stable at ~320ms, p99 down to ~900ms, will keep monitoring for 30m. if SLO burn returns we escalate to platform oncall
Alex T: thanks all. adding `postmortem:required` label on INC-9821. handing off to @jordan-l for the remainder of the oncall window :handshake:
Incident Bot: incident auto-resolve check scheduled in 30m
PagerDuty: incident status changed to: monitoring
